problems.title: Two Sum (Mastery Edition)
problems.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
hints: Hint 1: Can we trade space for time using an O(1) hash map lookup?
Hint 2: For each element x, compute complement = target - x.
Hint 3: Maintain single-pass hash map to achieve optimal O(N) time and O(N) space.
problems.explanation: Optimal linear pass using hash map tracking visited elements.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.description: Given an integer array `height` of length `n`, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the maximum water.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): The area between lines at left and right is (right - left) * min(height[left], height[right]).
Hint 2 (Intermediate): Start with left = 0 and right = n - 1 to maximize width.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Always move the pointer pointing to the shorter line inward, because keeping the shorter line can never yield a larger area.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Container With Most Water. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.description: Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where bar width is `1`, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Water above bar i equals min(left_max, right_max) - height[i].
Hint 2 (Advanced): Maintain left = 0, right = n - 1, left_max, and right_max.
Hint 3 (Advanced): If left_max < right_max, water at left is limited by left_max. Process left pointer and move right.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Trapping Rain Water. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Binary Search Target
problems.description: Given an array of integers `nums` sorted in ascending order, and an integer `target`, write a function to search `target` in `nums`. If target exists, return its index; otherwise, return `-1`.
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Maintain low = 0 and high = nums.length - 1.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Calculate mid = low + Math.floor((high - low) / 2).
Hint 3 (Beginner): If nums[mid] === target return mid. If nums[mid] < target set low = mid + 1, else high = mid - 1.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Binary Search Target. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: First & Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
problems.description: Given an array of integers `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending position of a given `target` value. If target is not found, return `[-1, -1]`.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Execute two distinct binary search functions: one for the leftmost index and one for the rightmost index.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): When nums[mid] === target in the left bound search, record index and continue searching left (high = mid - 1).
Hint 3 (Intermediate): For the right bound search, when nums[mid] === target, record index and continue searching right (low = mid + 1).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for First & Last Position of Element in Sorted Array. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.description: Given a rotated sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target` value, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or `-1` if it is not in `nums`.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): At any mid point, at least one half of the array (left half or right half) MUST be strictly sorted.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Determine if nums[l] <= nums[mid]. If true, left half is sorted; check if target lies within [nums[l], nums[mid]].
Hint 3 (Advanced): Otherwise, the right half is sorted; check if target lies within [nums[mid], nums[r]]. Adjust l and r accordingly.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Search in Rotated Sorted Array. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
problems.description: Given an array of positive integers `nums` and a positive integer `k`, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of size `k`.
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Compute the sum of the first k elements as your initial window sum.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Slide the window one element to the right by adding nums[i] and subtracting nums[i - k].
Hint 3 (Beginner): Keep track of the maximum window sum encountered during the iteration.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string `s`, find the length of the **longest substring** without repeating characters.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Use a sliding window defined by two pointers [left, right] and a Hash Set / Map to store characters in current window.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): As right pointer advances, if s[right] is already in set, shrink window by deleting s[left] and incrementing left.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Update max_length = max(max_length, right - left + 1) at each step.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.description: Given two strings `s` and `t` of lengths `m` and `n` respectively, return the **minimum window substring** of `s` such that every character in `t` (including duplicates) is included in the window. If no such substring exists, return empty string `""`.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Build target frequency map for t. Track `have` and `need` distinct character counts.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Expand right pointer. When s[right] satisfies target frequency requirement, increment `have`.
Hint 3 (Advanced): While `have === need`, record min length window and contract left pointer, updating `have` when a required character count drops.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Minimum Window Substring. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.description: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Anagrams share identical character frequencies. Can you sort each word to form a canonical key?
Hint 2 (Intermediate): Use a Hash Map mapping canonical_key -> list of matching original words.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Iterate through all strings, sort string chars (e.g. "eat" -> "aet"), append word to map[key], and return map values.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Group Anagrams. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals to `k`.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Subarray sum from i to j equals prefix_sum[j] - prefix_sum[i-1].
Hint 2 (Advanced): We need prefix_sum[j] - prefix_sum[i-1] == k => prefix_sum[i-1] == prefix_sum[j] - k.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Maintain rolling prefix sum and a Hash Map storing frequencies of previously seen prefix sums. Add map[current_prefix - k] to total count.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Subarray Sum Equals K. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle II
problems.description: Given the head of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If there is no cycle, return `null`.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Use fast and slow pointers. Fast moves 2 steps, slow moves 1 step. If they meet, a cycle exists.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): When fast and slow meet, reset slow to head. Keep fast at meeting point.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Move both slow and fast 1 step at a time. The node where they meet again is the exact start node of the cycle.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Linked List Cycle II. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

Hint 2 (Advanced): Alternatively, insert all list head nodes into a Min-Heap Priority Queue.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Repeatedly pop min node from heap, append to merged list, and push next node of popped list.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Merge K Sorted Lists. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): A node value must be strictly greater than ALL nodes in its left subtree and strictly less than ALL nodes in its right subtree.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): Pass valid min and max boundaries down the recursive helper function: validate(node, min, max).
Hint 3 (Intermediate): When going left, update max = node.val. When going right, update min = node.val.

problems.description: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize a string to a binary tree.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Use preorder traversal DFS for serialization, writing "N" for null nodes.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Join tokens into a comma-separated string (e.g. "1,2,N,N,3,4,N,N,5,N,N").
Hint 3 (Advanced): To deserialize, split string into queue. Recursively pop next token to build root, root.left, and root.right.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes `n` steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb `1` or `2` steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base cases: n = 1 -> 1 way, n = 2 -> 2 ways.
Hint 2 (Beginner): To reach step i, you could have come from step i-1 or step i-2.
Hint 3 (Beginner): Recurrence: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Store two previous values.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Climbing Stairs. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.description: You are given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount` representing a total amount of money. Return the **fewest number of coins** that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return `-1`.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Initialize dp array of size (amount + 1) filled with Infinity. dp[0] = 0.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): Loop i from 1 to amount. For each coin: if i - coin >= 0, dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - coin]).
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Return dp[amount] === Infinity ? -1 : dp[amount].
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Coin Change. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Edit Distance
problems.description: Given two strings `word1` and `word2`, return the minimum number of operations required to convert `word1` to `word2`. Allowed operations: Insert a character, Delete a character, Replace a character.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Build 2D DP grid where dp[i][j] is min operations to convert word1[0..i] to word2[0..j].
Hint 2 (Advanced): If word1[i-1] === word2[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1].
Hint 3 (Advanced): Otherwise, dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j] (delete), dp[i][j-1] (insert), dp[i-1][j-1] (replace)).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Edit Distance. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Flood Fill Grid
problems.description: An image is represented by an `m x n` integer grid `image` where `image[i][j]` represents the pixel value. Given starting pixel `(sr, sc)` and a new color `color`, perform a flood fill starting from `(sr, sc)`.
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def floodFill(self, image: List[List[int]], sr: int, sc: int, color: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        orig = image[sr][sc]
        if orig == color: return image
        R, C = len(image), len(image[0])
        def dfs(r, c):
            if r < 0 or r >= R or c < 0 or c >= C or image[r][c] != orig: return
            image[r][c] = color
            dfs(r+1, c); dfs(r-1, c); dfs(r, c+1); dfs(r, c-1)
        dfs(sr, sc)
        return image
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Save initial color = image[sr][sc]. If initial color === new color, return image immediately.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Write helper dfs(r, c) to check bounds and if image[r][c] === initial color.
Hint 3 (Beginner): Set image[r][c] = color, then recursively call dfs on (r+1, c), (r-1, c), (r, c+1), (r, c-1).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Flood Fill Grid. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.description: Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of `'1'`s (land) and `'0'`s (water), return the number of islands.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Iterate through every cell in the 2D grid.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): When encountering a '1', increment island count and launch a DFS/BFS traversal.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): During traversal, mark all connected '1' cells as '0' (sink the island) so they are not recounted.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Number of Islands. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Course Schedule II
problems.description: There are a total of `numCourses` courses you have to take. Given prerequisite pairs, return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all courses. If impossible due to a cycle, return `[]`.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Build adjacency list and track in-degree (number of prerequisites) for each node.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Push all nodes with in-degree == 0 into a BFS queue.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Pop queue, add node to result order, decrement in-degree of neighbors. If neighbor in-degree becomes 0, push to queue. If result length != numCourses, return [].
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Course Schedule II. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Given a string `s` containing just the characters `'(' `)' `'{' `'}' `'['` and `']'`, determine if the input string is valid.
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Maintain a LIFO stack array.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Push opening brackets '(', '{', '[' onto stack.
Hint 3 (Beginner): When encountering a closing bracket, pop stack and check if it matches the corresponding opening bracket. Return stack.length === 0 at end.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Valid Parentheses. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.description: Given an array of integers `temperatures` represents the daily temperatures, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` is the number of days you have to wait after the `i-th` day to get a warmer temperature. If there is no future day for which this is possible, keep `answer[i] == 0` instead.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Use a monotonic stack storing indices of days with decreasing temperatures.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): While stack is not empty and current temperature > temperatures[stack.top()], pop prev_index from stack.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Set answer[prev_index] = current_index - prev_index. Then push current_index onto stack.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Daily Temperatures. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.description: Given an array of integers `heights` representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is `1`, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Maintain a monotonic increasing stack storing pairs of (start_index, height).
Hint 2 (Advanced): When encountering a bar shorter than stack top, pop stack, calculate area = popped_height * (current_index - popped_index).
Hint 3 (Advanced): Extend the current bar's start_index backward to the last popped bar's index.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Largest Rectangle in Histogram. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
problems.description: Given an array `nums` with `n` objects colored red, white, or blue (represented as 0, 1, and 2), sort them **in-place** so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red, white, and blue.
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Maintain 3 pointers: low = 0, mid = 0, high = nums.length - 1.
Hint 2 (Beginner): If nums[mid] === 0, swap nums[low] and nums[mid], increment low and mid.
Hint 3 (Beginner): If nums[mid] === 1, increment mid. If nums[mid] === 2, swap nums[mid] and nums[high], decrement high.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array

problems.title: Two Sum — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Two Sum
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Two Sum — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Place left pointer at 0 and right pointer at len - 1.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): If numbers[left] + numbers[right] > target, decrement right pointer. Else increment left.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Return [left + 1, right + 1] when matching sum is found.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Group Anagrams — Level 2: Medium Sorted Array & O(1) Memory. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Group Anagrams — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Group Anagrams
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Group Anagrams — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Recursively compute leftDepth = maxDepth(node.left) and rightDepth = maxDepth(node.right).
Hint 3 (Beginner): Return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Invert Binary Tree — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Use a Queue to perform Breadth-First Search (BFS).
Hint 2 (Intermediate): At each step, record queue size to process all nodes at current depth level.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Append child nodes of current level to queue for next iteration.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Invert Binary Tree — Level 2: Medium Binary Tree Level Order Traversal. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree — Level 3: Hard Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.description: A **path** in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes has an edge connecting them. Return the **maximum path sum** of any non-empty path in the tree.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): At each node, max single path extending down is node.val + max(0, maxLeft, maxRight).
Hint 2 (Advanced): Local path combining left and right subtrees is node.val + max(0, left) + max(0, right).
Hint 3 (Advanced): Track global maximum across all local inverted V paths.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Invert Binary Tree — Level 3: Hard Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs — Level 1: Easy Climbing Stairs DP
problems.description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes `n` steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): dp[i] = number of ways to reach step i.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Recurrence: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2].
Hint 3 (Beginner): Base cases: dp[1] = 1, dp[2] = 2.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Climbing Stairs — Level 1: Easy Climbing Stairs DP. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs — Level 2: Medium Coin Change Minimum DP
problems.description: Given an integer array `coins` representing coins of different denominations and an integer `amount`, return the **fewest number of coins** needed to make up that amount. If impossible, return `-1`.
hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Initialize dp array of size (amount + 1) filled with amount + 1.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): Base case dp[0] = 0.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): For i from 1 to amount, dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - coin]) for each coin <= i.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Climbing Stairs — Level 2: Medium Coin Change Minimum DP. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs — Level 3: Hard Edit Distance (Levenshtein String DP)
problems.description: Given two strings `word1` and `word2`, return the **minimum number of operations** (insert, delete, replace character) required to convert `word1` into `word2` in **O(M * N)** time using 2D DP.
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Define dp[i][j] = edit distance between word1[0..i] and word2[0..j].
Hint 2 (Advanced): If word1[i] == word2[j], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1].
Hint 3 (Advanced): Otherwise dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j] (delete), dp[i][j-1] (insert), dp[i-1][j-1] (replace)).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Climbing Stairs — Level 3: Hard Edit Distance (Levenshtein String DP). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.title: Continuous Subarray Sum Prefix — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Continuous Subarray Sum Prefix
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Continuous Subarray Sum Prefix — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Same Tree Checker — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Task Scheduler Heap Execution
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

# Level 3 Hard Solution for Combination Sum Target
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:

problems.title: Power of X to N Recursion — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Power of X to N Recursion
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

# Level 3 Hard Solution for Permutations Generator
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]

                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

class Solution:

            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

        nums.sort()

            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.title: Find Pivot Index Prefix — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Find Pivot Index Prefix
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Find Pivot Index Prefix — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Traversal — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Recursively compute leftDepth = maxDepth(node.left) and rightDepth = maxDepth(node.right).
Hint 3 (Beginner): Return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth).

    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Recursively compute leftDepth = maxDepth(node.left) and rightDepth = maxDepth(node.right).
Hint 3 (Beginner): Return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth).

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Product of Array Except Self
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Product of Array Except Self — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Letter Combinations Phone
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:

                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:

problems.title: Relative Array Sorting — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Relative Array Sorting
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

problems.title: Trim Binary Search Tree — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])

# Level 3 Hard Solution for Range Sum Query Immutable
class Solution:

        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:

        return res

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

problems.title: Shifting Letters Prefix Sum — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Shifting Letters Prefix Sum
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Shifting Letters Prefix Sum — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Kth Smallest Matrix Heap
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])

problems.title: Tower of Hanoi Moves — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Tower of Hanoi Moves
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for N-Queens Board Placement
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

problems.title: Two Sum Sorted Array — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Two Sum Sorted Array
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Two Sum Sorted Array — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Symmetric Tree Checker — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Recursively compute leftDepth = maxDepth(node.left) and rightDepth = maxDepth(node.right).
Hint 3 (Beginner): Return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Symmetric Tree Checker — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])

problems.title: Matrix Block Sum 2D #2 — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Matrix Block Sum 2D #2
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Matrix Block Sum 2D #2 — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:

class Solution:

problems.title: Tower of Hanoi Moves (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Tower of Hanoi Moves (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Tower of Hanoi Moves (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])

problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.title: Multiply Strings Large Math (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Multiply Strings Large Math (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.

problems.title: Continuous Subarray Sum Prefix (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Continuous Subarray Sum Prefix (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Lemonade Change Greedy (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.title: Matrix Block Sum 2D (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Matrix Block Sum 2D (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Matrix Block Sum 2D (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Permutations Generator (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Permutations Generator (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

# Level 3 Hard Solution for Maximum Differences Query (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.title: Find Pivot Index Prefix (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Find Pivot Index Prefix (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Find Pivot Index Prefix (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

hints: Hint 1 (Intermediate): Place left pointer at 0 and right pointer at len - 1.
Hint 2 (Intermediate): If numbers[left] + numbers[right] > target, decrement right pointer. Else increment left.
Hint 3 (Intermediate): Return [left + 1, right + 1] when matching sum is found.

problems.title: Matchsticks to Square (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Matchsticks to Square (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Matchsticks to Square (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Construct BST Preorder (Medium) — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
hints: Hint 1 (Beginner): Base case: if node is null, depth is 0.
Hint 2 (Beginner): Recursively compute leftDepth = maxDepth(node.left) and rightDepth = maxDepth(node.right).
Hint 3 (Beginner): Return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth).
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Construct BST Preorder (Medium) — Level 1: Easy Maximum Depth of Binary Tree. Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

# Level 3 Hard Solution for Recursive Combination Sum (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:

                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])

    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Subarray Sum Equals K Prefix (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

problems.description: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree `root` (where nulls represent empty nodes), return its **maximum depth** (number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf).
problems.solutionCode:
class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0
        # Level order array depth calculation
        import math
        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0

problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Boat Saved People Greedy (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res

Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

problems.title: Range Sum Query Immutable (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Range Sum Query Immutable (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Range Sum Query Immutable (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

problems.title: Generate Parentheses Combo (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum)
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return all unique triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j != k` and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`. The solution set must **contain no duplicate triplets**.
problems.solutionCode:
# Level 3 Hard Solution for Generate Parentheses Combo (Medium)
class Solution:
    def solveLevel3(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        nums.sort()
        res = []
        for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
            if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue
            l, r = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
            while l < r:
                s = nums[i] + nums[l] + nums[r]
                if s == 0:
                    res.append([nums[i], nums[l], nums[r]])
                    while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l + 1]: l += 1
                    while l < r and nums[r] == nums[r - 1]: r -= 1
                    l += 1; r -= 1
                elif s < 0: l += 1
                else: r -= 1
        return res
hints: Hint 1 (Advanced): Sort the input array nums first to easily skip duplicates and use two pointers.
Hint 2 (Advanced): Iterate i from 0 to N-3. Place left = i + 1 and right = N - 1.
Hint 3 (Advanced): Increment left or decrement right to match sum. When sum == 0, skip identical adjacent elements.
problems.explanation: Algorithmic approach and walkthrough for Generate Parentheses Combo (Medium) — Level 3: Hard Zero-Sum Triplets (3Sum). Optimal time complexity is achieved using standard algorithmic patterns.

class Solution:

class Solution:

class Solution:
    def solveLevel1(self, root: List[Optional[int]]) -> int:
        if not root or root[0] is None: return 0

        valid_count = len([x for x in root if x is not None])
        return int(math.log2(valid_count)) + 1 if valid_count else 0
